title: Would anybody be willing to make a Black and White Clone?
author: Dangerous_Three_8506
selftext:
The old game by Peter Molyneux. Not number 2, but number 1.

I would love you so much if you made it and put it on Github for me to play with the code. I would be so happy. Made with Astra of course!

It was my birthday 1 week ago, does that count?

I played that game everyday for years, I also wanted to mod it but it wasn't really feasible at the time.

If this is an inappropriate post just let me know, I apologize in advance. I was told its better to ask forgiveness rather than permission for some things. This is one of them.

What a time to be alive. Video games and Studios being made in the 10000s everyday. Its so awesome.

The studio creation is honest to god the coolest experience. "GPT, lets work with Claude and remake Photoshop and Spine and Blender but for me."

"Lets make scripts for very open-source studio and see what you can do!!!"

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body:
Create a polished, 3D god-game identical to the classic creature-training god game Black & White.



Working title: “Eden's Lift”



CORE FANTASY



The player is an embodied spirit watching over a living island. The player interacts directly with the world through a large visible hand, gains influence through belief, develops settlements, performs supernatural acts, and raises a giant intelligent creature whose behavior changes according to how the player treats and teaches it. \[Refer to CreatureInt.Txt for how to make the creature\]



The experience should support benevolent, pragmatic, destructive, and mixed play styles without assigning morality through simplistic dialogue choices. Alignment must emerge from the player’s repeated actions and their consequences.



TARGET VERTICAL SLICE



Build one polished, replayable island containing:



\- Two culturally distinct villages

\- 40–60 simulated villagers

\- One trainable giant creature

\- One rival supernatural guardian

\- At least six miracles

\- Resource production and construction

\- Village belief and influence systems

\- Moral and visual alignment

\- A tutorial integrated into play

\- One central conflict with several possible resolutions

\- Approximately 30–45 minutes of polished gameplay



Use Blender for editable 3D assets and Godot 4 for the playable game unless the existing project already uses another suitable engine.



PLAYER INTERACTION



Represent the cursor as a fully animated divine hand.



The hand must be able to:



\- Move freely across the terrain

\- Point at and highlight valid targets

\- Pick up and drop physical objects

\- Throw rocks and other suitable objects

\- Collect and distribute food and wood

\- Move villagers only when the design permits it

\- Pet, reward, discipline, and guide the creature

\- Cast miracles through clear mouse gestures

\- Interact with buildings, trees, water, and environmental objects

\- Produce strong visual, audio, and haptic-style feedback for every action



Make grabbing, carrying, dropping, throwing, and gesture recognition feel reliable before expanding the rest of the game. Avoid pixel-perfect gestures; recognize intent using tolerant direction, distance, speed, and shape thresholds. Provide accessible button alternatives for every gesture.



CAMERA



Create a seamless strategy camera that feels like physically navigating a miniature world:



\- Pan by dragging the terrain

\- Orbit smoothly around a selected point

\- Zoom continuously from an island overview to an intimate village view

\- Preserve the point beneath the cursor while zooming

\- Prevent clipping through terrain and buildings

\- Smooth sudden transitions without introducing noticeable input delay

\- Provide camera reset, focus, and bookmark controls



The camera and hand must remain responsive at all supported frame rates.



LIVING VILLAGE SIMULATION



Every villager should have:



\- A name, age group, household, role, home, needs, health, beliefs, and current task

\- Hunger, rest, safety, social, spiritual, and work priorities

\- A readable daily routine

\- Reactions to miracles, danger, abundance, destruction, and the creature

\- Memory of significant player actions

\- Limited local knowledge rather than global omniscience



Villagers should gather food and wood, construct buildings, maintain homes, worship, form households, respond to emergencies, and communicate important needs to the player.



Use utility-based decision-making or another inspectable system. Avoid expensive individual planning every frame. Update distant or inactive villagers at reduced frequencies while preserving believable outcomes.



CREATURE  \[Refer to CreatureInt.Txt for more on the creature\]



Design an original giant creature named the “Morrow,” visually distinct from any Black & White creature. Begin with three selectable original species concepts—for example, a bullfrog, an avian river guardian, and a six-limbed stoneback—and let me choose before producing the final model.



The creature must:



\- Navigate the island without frequent pathfinding failures

\- Eat, sleep, play, explore, help, resist, and become distracted

\- Learn associations between situations and player reactions

\- Observe and imitate selected player actions

\- Remember rewarded and discouraged behaviors

\- Develop preferences and habits

\- Express needs and emotions through posture, face, sound, and movement

\- Grow visually and behaviorally during the scenario

\- Help or harm villagers according to what it has learned

\- Sometimes make understandable mistakes instead of behaving perfectly



Implement learning as a transparent system that can be inspected and tuned. Track behavior tendencies such as generosity, aggression, curiosity, obedience, independence, playfulness, and protectiveness.



Reward and discipline must alter tendencies gradually. One accidental input must not permanently redefine the creature. Show learning through animation and behavior, not constant numerical popups.



MORAL ALIGNMENT



Track alignment from actions and consequences rather than explicit good-or-evil buttons.



Relevant actions include:



\- Feeding or starving settlements

\- Healing or harming inhabitants

\- Protecting or frightening villagers

\- Sharing or hoarding resources

\- Respecting or coercing rival communities

\- Teaching the creature care or cruelty

\- Using destructive miracles when safer alternatives exist



Alignment should gradually affect:



\- The divine hand

\- The creature’s appearance and behavior

\- Village architecture and decoration

\- Ambient color and weather

\- Music layers and environmental audio

\- Vegetation and wildlife

\- Villager reactions



Use an original visual language. Do not reproduce Black & White’s angel/devil advisers or its exact good-and-evil appearance changes.



BELIEF AND INFLUENCE



Villages generate belief based on safety, prosperity, awe, cultural expectations, remembered interventions, and fear.



Belief powers miracles and expands an influence field around settlements and sacred structures. Powerful actions should cost belief or require suitable conditions. Prevent infinite-resource loops and miracle spam.



Fear may create fast obedience but unstable loyalty. Trust should grow more slowly and remain more resilient. Neither approach should be an automatic winning strategy.



MIRACLES



Implement six original miracles:



1. Verdant Pulse — accelerates crops and restores damaged vegetation.

2. Wellspring — creates a temporary source of clean water.

3. Mending Light — heals living targets within a small area.

4. Gale Hand — pushes objects, enemies, smoke, and projectiles.

5. Emberfall — creates controlled fire that can spread if mishandled.

6. Skybreak — calls a dangerous localized storm.



Each miracle needs:



\- A distinct gesture and accessible button binding

\- Clear targeting previews

\- Belief cost and cooldown rules

\- Visual and audio feedback

\- Beneficial and harmful uses

\- Interactions with terrain, buildings, villagers, resources, and the creature

\- Automated tests for valid targets, invalid targets, cost, cancellation, and edge cases



CENTRAL SCENARIO



A drought threatens both villages. One community controls an ancient reservoir, while the other occupies fertile farmland downstream. The rival guardian encourages coercion and conflict.



Support several systemic resolutions:



\- Restore the watershed through environmental miracles

\- Negotiate resource sharing by earning both villages’ trust

\- Intimidate the reservoir village into releasing water

\- Use the creature to transport supplies and repair infrastructure

\- Destroy the rival guardian’s power base

\- Allow one community to dominate the other

\- Discover an additional solution through interacting systems



Do not reduce the scenario to a single scripted choice. Let the simulation recognize meaningful player strategies and produce appropriate consequences.



BLENDER ASSET PIPELINE



Use Blender’s Python API to create and maintain editable source assets.



Create:



\- The three creature concepts and final selected creature

\- Modular village buildings for two original cultures

\- Temple and influence structures

\- Trees, rocks, crops, tools, storage, food, and construction props

\- Hand model and animations

\- Terrain dressing

\- Miracle-related objects and effects meshes

\- Collision and navigation proxy meshes

\- Creature skeleton, facial controls, and animation set

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body:
**I couldn't paste the whole thing, too many characters!**

Maintain consistent scale, pivots, orientation, naming, collections, material slots, and export settings.



For every runtime asset:



\- Apply or intentionally preserve transforms

\- Validate normals and manifold requirements

\- Generate UVs

\- Provide appropriate collision

\- Limit material batches

\- Establish polygon and texture budgets

\- Add LODs where beneficial

\- Export through a repeatable automated pipeline

\- Preserve the editable .blend source



Before final integration, render the creature and architectural assets from several angles and inspect silhouette, deformation, materials, scale, and visual cohesion.



ART DIRECTION



Use a colorful storybook-mythic style with hand-shaped terrain, broad readable forms, painterly materials, warm daylight, dramatic weather, and subtle magical luminescence.



The world should feel inviting from a distance and richly animated up close. Use an original palette centered on jade vegetation, pale limestone, oxidized copper, amber magic, and indigo storms.



Prioritize:



\- Readable silhouettes

\- Expressive animation

\- Strong differences between the two village cultures

\- Clear feedback for interactable objects

\- Visual changes caused by simulation and alignment

\- Stable performance over photorealism



AUDIO



Create an original adaptive audio design specification covering:



\- Village activity

\- Creature emotions

\- Miracle casting

\- Weather

\- Moral alignment

\- Rival presence

\- Hand interactions

\- Alerts and interface feedback



Use only original, licensed, or public-domain audio. Do not imitate Black & White’s soundtrack, voices, or signature sound effects.



DEVELOPMENT PROCESS



Work autonomously and preserve a playable build throughout development.



Milestone 1: Write a concise design document, technical architecture, performance budget, and risk register.



Milestone 2: Build a gray-box island with final-feeling camera and hand controls.



Milestone 3: Implement one village, basic needs, resource gathering, construction, and belief.



Milestone 4: Implement the creature with navigation, needs, expressions, training, and inspectable learning state.



Milestone 5: Implement all six miracles and their systemic interactions.



Milestone 6: Add the second village, rival guardian, drought scenario, and multiple resolutions.



Milestone 7: Create and integrate the Blender art, animations, materials, collisions, and LODs.



Milestone 8: Add interface, accessibility, audio hooks, save/load, tutorials, alignment presentation, and polish.



Milestone 9: Optimize, test, package, and document the vertical slice.



After each milestone:



\- Launch and play the current build

\- Capture representative screenshots

\- Inspect runtime state

\- Record performance

\- Identify and repair the highest-impact problems

\- Preserve previous working versions

\- Update a short progress and decision log



TESTABILITY



Add named test scenarios for:



\- Hand grabbing and throwing

\- Camera navigation

\- Villager hunger and resource collection

\- Building construction

\- Belief gain and loss

\- Influence boundaries

\- Every miracle

\- Creature reward and discipline

\- Creature imitation

\- Creature navigation through villages

\- Drought progression

\- Each intended scenario resolution

\- Saving and reloading

\- Low-resource and high-population conditions



Expose a development panel showing:



\- Selected villager or creature state

\- Current goals and decision scores

\- Belief and alignment changes with reasons

\- Navigation path

\- Simulation speed

\- Population and job counts

\- Draw calls, triangle counts, memory, and frame timing



Create deterministic seeds and reproducible starting states. A screenshot is not sufficient proof that a system works; test the actual state transitions and player journey.



QUALITY REQUIREMENTS



Target Windows desktop, keyboard and mouse, 1080p, and a stable 60 FPS on a mid-range gaming PC.



The vertical slice is complete only when:



\- The camera and divine hand feel responsive

\- The primary interactions are discoverable and reliable

\- Villagers complete believable daily routines

\- The creature visibly learns at least five behaviors

\- All miracles interact correctly with the simulation

\- The scenario supports at least four substantially different resolutions

\- Saving and loading preserves the world accurately

\- The game runs for 30 minutes without critical errors

\- No placeholder asset is visible in the packaged build

\- Automated checks pass

\-

\- A clean machine can launch the packaged build



Do not claim that a feature works merely because its code exists. Verify it by playing the relevant sequence and inspecting its resulting state.



When a requirement conflicts with stability or performance, preserve the core fantasy in this priority order:



1. Hand interaction

2. Creature relationship and learning

3. Living village simulation

4. Moral consequences

5. Miracles

6. Visual richness

7. Additional content



Make reasonable decisions without pausing for minor preferences. Ask only when a missing decision would fundamentally change the project. Continue until the packaged vertical slice and its source files are complete.

replies.author: Interesting-Act-1958
replies.body:
I didn’t mention game mechanics or claim that mechanics are protected by copyright. I said that making a straight clone of a still-licensed commercial game raises legal and ethical questions. Whether particular mechanics can be copyrighted doesn’t settle either of those broader questions.  

Black & White took roughly three years to develop and involved substantial original work in adaptive creature AI, gesture control, animation blending, moral transformation of the world, and interface design. 

The ethical issue is not “old mechanics must never be reused.” It is whether deliberately making a 1:1 replacement fairly respects the creative labour, distinctive expression, attribution, and continuing interests behind the original, particularly when less appropriative preservation approaches are available.

You’re free to reach a different ethical conclusion. But “nothing in ethics says you can’t” is an unsupported assertion, not a rebuttal, and telling me to grow up doesn’t make it one.
